transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-06
Time: 10:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Marcus (Redwood AE), Sofia (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena March, Jasper Cole, Priya Nair
Links referenced: https://redwood.ai/poc/orchidum/benchmarks (lab sheet), https://redwood.ai/security-pack (security docs)

Auto-summary (auto gen, may be imperfect):
- Reviewed last week's bench run: Redwood Dedicated candidate vs incumbent provider (IncumbentAI).
- Observed lower p50 token latency on Redwood in steady-state for medium-length prompts, but IncumbentAI had better short-burst tail under their tuned infra.
- Discussed routing decisions, quantization tradeoffs, prefix/KV cache warm-up effects, and next stress tests.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Marcus (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate the time. Quick roll call, then we'll jump into the bench numbers. Sofia and I pulled the updated runs from the lab sheet, um, if anyone doesn't have it I can re-share after.
[00:00:22] Dr. Elena: Got it, I can see the sheet. Jasper's on audio-only, Priya is hopping in at 10:15.
[00:00:30] Marcus: Perfect. Objective for today: compare the throughput/latency deltas vs your incumbent, and agree an action plan for the 2-hour stress that you asked for.
[00:00:44] Jasper: Sounds good. Quick refresh — our incumbent (IncumbentAI) is running on CloudVendorX c8i-like instances, with a custom batching service. We generally see 18–22 RPS at 95% latency under production mix.
[00:00:58] Sofia (SE): Thanks, Jasper. We ran two main configs: Redwood hosted candidate (quantized int8-ish runtime with selective KV cache), and a Redwood Dedicated slot with our throughput-tuned kernel selection. The sheet has p50/p95/p99 across short (<=64 tokens) and medium (65–512 tokens) cohorts.
[00:01:20] Dr. Elena: Can you call out the headline numbers first — we skimmed and got a bit turned around.
[00:01:26] Sofia: Sure. Headline: for medium prompts, Redwood Dedicated steady-state p50 token latency was about 22% lower than your incumbent; p95 was roughly comparable (within 10%). For short prompts, incumbent had slightly better tail under burst — likely due to their micro-batching trick and rate-shaping.
[00:01:50] Marcus: Important caveat: our lab runs used prefix/KV warmup for the medium cohort — if the cache isn't warm, the delta changes. We included cold-start rows in the sheet to show that.
[00:02:05] Jasper: Hmm. The cold-start numbers are what we worry about because our traffic is spiky — lots of sessions with new prefixes.
[00:02:12] Sofia: Right, and that's why routing and fallback matter. Two options we discussed in the lab: 1) route short, cold sessions to a lower-latency incumbent path (cost higher), 2) use a small pool of warmed dedicated slots as a fast-path for new prefixes.
[00:02:30] Dr. Elena: Can Redwood do a warmed pool? That was our earlier ask — having a small hot set to handle spikes.
[00:02:36] Marcus: Yes — we can reserve dedicated slots and keep a warmed KV cache. There is cost involved but for a pilot we can do a constrained size. Sofia, remind them about the autoscaling cooldowns and slot burst behaviour.
[00:02:48] Sofia: Sure — for Dedicated we recommend a steady baseline plus a short-burst buffer. Autoscale cooldown is 60–90s in our default; we can tune down to 30s in pilot but that risks more GPU churn. Also, the kernel selection for short sequences uses a different math kernel; we can enable an optimized path that reduces p50 further by ~8% on short requests, at the expense of slightly higher cost per token.
[00:03:15] Jasper: That's interesting — can you quantify the cost delta?
[00:03:18] Marcus: We'll put numbers in the sheet. Ballpark: optimized short-path might increase tokens/sec cost by ~12% for those bursts, but if it reduces retries and improves user-perceived latency you may consider it net positive.
[00:03:32] Priya (CTO): We care about predictable latency SLOs more than marginal cost for now. If Redwood can show consistent p95 under 350ms for our medium prompts at 50 RPS, that's a win.
[00:03:43] Sofia: Understood. Our current Dedicated run hit p95 ~310ms for medium at 45 RPS sustained in the lab. We'll try the tuned knob set for 50 RPS in the stress window.
[00:03:55] Marcus: Also noted we saw an odd oscillation in throughput on the incumbent baseline around minute 18 in their published log — looks like they hit a rate limiter or a jittery autoscale. We flagged it in the sheet and added the raw logs link.
[00:04:10] Jasper: Yeah, their autoscaler is source-of-truth and it's... finicky. We wanted a second vendor as backup but cost tradeoffs are real.
[00:04:18] Dr. Elena: On security/compliance: Priya, you asked for SOC2 and KMS notes last week — Marcus, can you confirm what Redwood will hand over?
[00:04:27] Marcus: Yep — we'll send the security pack link after the call. It includes SOC2 Type II summary, KMS/HSM integration notes, per-token observability, and audit log exports. Note: for Private/VPC we can offer customer-managed keys.
[00:04:40] Jasper: Good. One more infra question — does Redwood's KV cache persist across restarts? We had trouble with cold cache after node rebuilds.
[00:04:49] Sofia: By default the KV is in-memory per pod; for Dedicated we offer a persistent checkpoint mechanism so cache warm-up can be faster after node restarts. There's an additional small latency during checkpoint writes but usually worth it for fewer cold windows.
[00:05:03] Priya: Ok. On benchmarks, I want to make sure the dataset of prompts accurately reflects our 95th percentiles — we'll send the sample set later today.
[00:05:10] Marcus: Great. For the stress test: propose Redwood runs a 2-hour sustained test at 50 RPS with production prompt mix, we stream logs, and then we do a joint postmortem. When would you like that?
[00:05:21] Jasper: Could we do it Friday night (May 7) after traffic window? We'll provide the exact 95th-percentile prompt list by tomorrow.
[00:05:27] Marcus: Friday night works for us; we'll need a 1-hour lead to provision the dedicated slot and confirm compilation flags.
[00:05:33] Sofia: Also calling out quantization notes — we tested both int8 and a mixed-precision path. Mixed-precision gave slightly better p95 but a higher memory footprint. For the 2-hour stress we suggest mixed-precision to avoid token drops under long contexts, unless you want stricter cost control.
[00:05:52] Dr. Elena: Mixed precision sounds safer for the pilot. We'll take the cost delta if it improves stability.
[00:05:57] Marcus: Noted. On routing playbook — we sketched a fallback: if p95 breaches target for 2 consecutive minutes, route new requests to warmed incumbents (if enabled) or spin up an extra dedicated slot. We'll include exact thresholds in the playbook doc.
[00:06:12] Jasper: Do you have a sample playbook we can review?
[00:06:15] Sofia: Yes — link in the sheet. We'll push a condensed playbook to the CRM.
[00:06:20] [discussion and multi-speaker crosstalk, 06:20–18:00 — tuning knobs and command snippets]
[00:18:05] Marcus: Quick demo of the curl run we executed, I'm pasting the command in chat. Example uses token-batching headers and explicit kernel flag --fast-short. The output shows p50/p95 for that short cohort.
[00:18:22] Jasper: I see the output, few typos in the sample but interpretable.
[00:18:35] Sofia: Right — occasional transcription noise in the auto logs; ignore the 'k v cash' typos, that's KV cache.
[00:18:42] Marcus: We also noted request-level tracing IDs — we'll give you a mapping so you can correlate your app logs with our traces.
[00:18:49] Dr. Elena: Excellent, that helps our SREs.
[00:18:55] [silence while Marcus shares links]
[00:19:30] Priya: A question on contractual terms — if we go Dedicated pilot and we like it, what's the minimum commit?
[00:19:38] Marcus: For pilot we can offer a no-commit 30-day trial on a reduced-rate dedicated slot. If you convert we have standard reserved capacity tiers, but we can discuss an enterprise term later.
[00:19:50] Priya: Ok. We'll need legal to look at the data residency clause.
[00:19:54] Marcus: We'll include region and data-handling notes in the security pack.
[00:20:00] [discussion on logs and observability, 20:00–30:00 — Jasper asks for token-level cost breakdowns per route]
[00:30:15] Sofia: Quick note — the Redwood Optimize suggestions in the sheet recommend a quant schedule: int8 for background batch jobs, mixed-precision for user-facing low-latency paths. We simulated token-cost impact; it's in the sheet.
[00:30:32] Jasper: That scheduling makes sense.
[00:30:38] Marcus: Alright, let's align on concrete next steps: 1) Jasper sends the 95th-percentile prompt set by EOD tomorrow (05/07). 2) Redwood provisions dedicated slot and shares stress window details by 05/08. 3) Joint 2-hour stress test Friday 05/07 night — wait slight mismatch, Marcus: we need to provision before Friday — propose we move stress test to Saturday 05/08 01:00–03:00 UTC to be safe.
[00:31:05] Jasper: Saturday 01:00–03:00 UTC works. We'll confirm.
[00:31:12] Dr. Elena: Post-test, can Redwood give a short written readout and a recommended routing policy?
[00:31:18] Sofia: Yes — we'll deliver a 1-page readout and an annotated playbook within 48 hours of the test.
[00:31:24] Marcus: Great. Any final questions?
[00:31:28] Priya: One last ask — include an example of the fallback metrics that would trigger escalation to our incident channel.
[00:31:33] Marcus: Will do.
[00:31:36] [wrap-up and social]
[00:31:50] Marcus: Thanks everyone. We'll send the stub playbook, the security pack, and the provisioning checklist after the call.
[00:32:00] Jasper: Thanks, talk soon.
[00:32:05] Dr. Elena: Appreciate it.

Call end ~52:00

Notes and quirks:
- Transcription occasionally labels 'KV' as 'k v' and model names get fuzzed (e.g., 'Redood' instead of Redwood).
- Several technical snippets were shared (curl examples, kernel flags, and log bundles). See lab sheet for the exact commands.
- Action items captured above; we also saved an inline playbook draft in the lab sheet.
